extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, researchers, and research-integrity stakeholders (readers of Retraction Watch)
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and responding to weaknesses in journal editorial handling and peer review (especially in guest-edited special issues) that can indicate fraud, paper-mill activity, or other integrity breaches. The page discusses specific red flags, detection tools, and consequences (bulk retraction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher’s investigation found the guest editor for the issue selected the peer reviewers, the majority of whom were affiliated with Nanjing University in China.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid allowing guest editors (or authors) to unilaterally select reviewers; ensure reviewer selection is independent and balanced. Monitor reviewer affiliation concentration and conflicts of interest as part of reviewer assignment. The page treats reviewer selection by a guest editor plus affiliation clustering as a direct indicator of compromised review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of compromised peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation found 'evidence of compromised peer review in almost all articles' and the journal concluded the review process was 'irreparably compromised.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate any signals of compromised review thoroughly; if the peer-review process is irreparably compromised, consider retraction. Use investigation findings (e.g., reviewer identity/behavior, timeline anomalies) as grounds for corrective action and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improbable device use / experimental independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The retraction notice refers to 'evidence of improbable device use in many articles' — explained as 'the type of issue that arises when the same device is used by two people who are supposed to be entirely independent of each other.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify provenance and independence of equipment/devices/data sources claimed to be independent. Treat identical device identifiers, improbable reuse of specialized equipment across independent studies, or other provenance anomalies as red flags for data integrity problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope appropriateness and editorial regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor-in-chief Huw Dorkins said: 'This topic collection was really out of scope for the journal, and accepted under a different editorial regime, when different processes applied.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure topic collections and special issues align with journal scope and are handled under the journal’s standard editorial policies and oversight. If different editorial regimes are used, put compensating controls in place (e.g., additional oversight, independent checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues (guest-edited) are high-risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states 'Guest-edited special issues appear to be particularly vulnerable to paper mills,' and cites multiple publishers retracting many papers or suspending special issues because of 'compromised articles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat guest-edited special issues as higher risk: apply heightened scrutiny (stricter reviewer vetting, editorial oversight, audits) or limit guest-edited formats. Consider temporary suspension or policy changes if systemic problems are detected, as some publishers have done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt analytic detection tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems 'came to light via tools that highlight potential problems in published articles,' and those tools 'only became available in the past 2-3 years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and routinely use analytic/detection tools that flag suspicious patterns (e.g., reviewer networks, device reuse, text similarity, authorship clusters). Keep detection capabilities up to date and integrate them into editorial workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation concentration and repeated co-authorship as red flags
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the authors on the retracted papers listed affiliations with institutions in China, including Nanjing University, and several co-authored more than one article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor for unusual concentrations of author affiliations or repeated co-authorship across multiple papers in the same issue; such clustering can indicate coordinated or fraudulent submissions and should prompt further scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and clarity in retraction communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher's investigation was summarized in a retraction notice; the publisher declined to name the guest editor citing policy/legal concerns, and an embargoed notice was accidentally published early due to a technical mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, timely retraction notices that explain reasons to the extent legally permissible while balancing confidentiality/legal constraints. Maintain strict controls over embargoed communications to avoid premature publication and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust editorial-handling controls and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece references multiple incidents where journals retracted papers for 'compromised editorial handling and peer review process' and notes the journal has 'reviewed our policies and improved our practice around topic collections.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain robust editorial policies and oversight for handling submissions, especially for nonstandard formats (topic collections, guest-edited issues). Regularly review and update policies in response to detected vulnerabilities and industry incidents; ensure consistent application of editorial standards.
